s1.raw:
DOES NOT ACCOUNT -- "The house of David is told here of Joseph."

The TAKES sentence only says whom the phrase "of the house of David" is told of. It gives no meaning for the witness words and does not say how the position agrees with them. It also does not join the witness to Matthew 1:20-21 or any other verse.

s2.raw: DOES NOT ACCOUNT -- "The house of David is told here of Joseph."

s1.raw:
DOES NOT ACCOUNT -- ""His own body" is the body proper to the kind, and the kind is one flesh of men."

The TAKES words quote "his own body" and give it a meaning ("the body proper to the kind"). But they never join that meaning to the witness's other words, "God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him" or "to every seed". The rest of the sentence, "the kind is one flesh of men", is the position's conclusion. It is not a reading of this verse's words, and it does not say how the position agrees with them, so it does not account for the witness.

s2.raw:
DOES NOT ACCOUNT -- "\"His own body\" is the body proper to the kind, and the kind is one flesh of men."

The TAKES words do restate the phrase "his own body" and give it a meaning, "the body proper to the kind". But they never join that meaning to the rest of the witness, "God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every seed his own body". They do not connect it to seed, to God giving the body, or to any other verse. "The kind is one flesh of men" is the position's conclusion, and the TAKES words do not show how the witness's own words lead to it.

s1.raw:
DOES NOT ACCOUNT -- "David's fruit therefore reaches him as flesh through a woman of David's line."

The TAKES sentence states a conclusion about how David's fruit reaches him. It does not quote or take up the words "Of the fruit of thy body" or "set upon thy throne". It does not give a meaning for "fruit of thy body", with "body" glossed as belly (H990), and it does not say how the position agrees with those words. It does not join the witness to Romans 1:3 or Galatians 4:4 either.
